drawings.description: une boucle et quelques points, avec des flèches à double pointe partant d'un sommet, étiquetées $x$ et $xg$ ; au-dessous « Diagramme de Cayley » et un encadré « $g$, $g'$, $gh$ » ; une seconde boucle et deux flèches horizontales vers la gauche.
drawings.kind: Cayley diagram sketch: loop, points, double-headed arrows
drawings.notes: The lower half of p. 36 is written upside down; crop rotated 180 degrees and redrawn upright on a tight crop. The box (now drawn) with its contents kept as the transcription reads them, g, g', gh (on the crop they read like g, g_1, ..., g_k); two horizontal arrows to its right, the first with a single head in its middle, the second with a double head (>>) near its start; "Diagramme de Cayley". The loop starts and ends at a vertex, passing through a second vertex above it; the arrows are double-pointed in the sense of two chevrons (>>), not heads at both ends as drawn before: from the upper vertex to the right, and from the lower vertex along the straight stroke xg to its point, and down to the right (x); a short tail down to the left. Points: the vertex, the end of xg, two at the far left, a row of three to the right; the second loop on the right ends at g. Left out: the three long oblique strokes crossing the region (read as strikes; drawn grey before), the upside-down sentence at the bottom (text), the typed text showing through. Still a reading: the box contents and the double heads (rendered with two Stealth tips). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the arrows carry double chevrons (>>) along the stroke, as the legend of two arrows beside the box shows (one with a single head, one with a double head); drawn so already. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the box reads G, g_1, [gap], g_k (a large first letter, then indexed g's; the line « Mot en les g_i + origine » under the figure has the same g_i), not g, g', gh; the label is corrected, with the gap left as on the page; the transcription's reading is to be corrected there. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the three long oblique strokes run far beyond the figure, across the box corner, the caption and the lines below: they cancel this part of the sheet and are not part of the Cayley diagram; they stay left out. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 259 ppi colour scan (rendered at 350 dpi, crop turned 180 degrees). Changed: the loop redrawn through points read on its ink (its right end was up to 0.7 unit off); the heavy dot of the upper vertex added; the second, inner stroke between the two vertices added, with the arrowhead pointing up that stands between it and the loop (drawn on the inner stroke: on the page it straddles both); the double chevrons placed where they stand (mid-stroke on the upper arrow, near the start of xg, near the end of x), and the second legend arrow's two chevrons at 61.4 and 63; the small dot at (62.7, 39) and the short thin tail of the dot left of g added; the labels x, xg, g moved onto their ink; the second loop redrawn through its ink. Every element now lies on the ink to within about 0.5 unit. Left out as before: the three long oblique strokes that cancel this part of the sheet, the upside-down sentence, the typed text showing through, and a faint grey stroke with specks below the two left points (about (7, 54) to (14.5, 48.5)), which reads as show-through, not as ink of the figure.
drawings.orientation: upside down on the page (tete-beche half); crop rotated 180 degrees, redraw upright, coordinates in the rotated crop

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, un quadrant d'axes avec des points disposés en escalier sous la diagonale, figurant les bidegrés $(i,j)$, $j \le i$, où le morphisme est un isomorphisme.
drawings.kind: quadrant with staircase of points below the diagonal
drawings.notes: In the left margin: two axes from a small open origin, and heavy points in a staircase below the diagonal (bidegrees (i, j), j <= i), columns of 2, 3, 4 and 5 points; some points heavier than others.

drawings.description: à gauche, un schéma à traits sans flèches\,: $k$ relié par $u$, $u'$, $u''$ à $\Phi$, $\Phi'$ (écrit deux fois, un tracé biffé), $\Phi''$\,; $\Phi,\Phi'$ vers $N$, $\Phi',\Phi''$ vers $N'$, puis $N$ et $N'$ vers $N''$
drawings.notes: k joined by u, u', u'' to Phi, the first Phi', Phi''; Phi and the first Phi' to N, the second Phi' and Phi'' to N'; N and N' to N''. Omitted as struck: the stroke from k to the second Phi' (scribbled over on the page), so the second Phi' has no stroke from k. The small u labels are tiny and placed by eye. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the first Phi' already carries the stroke u' from k, and the second Phi' is the same object written again for N', so leaving out the struck stroke loses no relation; the drawing stays as it is. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.kind: square of arrows between C^*_*, C^*_bullet, C^bullet_bullet, C^bullet_*
drawings.notes: Four nodes in a diamond: C^*_* (top), C^*_bullet (left), C^bullet_bullet (bottom), C^bullet_* = Lambda^{bullet+1} Phi_* (right), with arrows: top to left (heavy), left to bottom, bottom to right, and a double-headed arrow right - top. The braces of formulas beside the nodes are text.
drawings.disagreement: The transcription calls 17-2 and 17-3 "hexagones": on the page each is a diamond of four nodes and four arrows.

drawings.notes: The dual diamond: C_*^* = C^{*vee}_* (top), C_*^bullet = C^{bullet vee}_* (left), C_bullet^bullet = C^{bullet vee}_bullet (bottom), and on the right C^*_bullet = C^vee_{bullet *} (as read); arrows top to left, right to top, right to bottom, and left to bottom (heavy). Node labels as read on the crop (the transcription does not spell them).

drawings.description: sous deux crochets illisibles, un faisceau de segments reliant deux colonnes de points : l’image d’un shuffle.
drawings.kind: shuffle: segments between two columns of points
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop. Nine strokes between a left column of five marks and a right column of five marks (drawn as points): the four upper ones descend steeply to the right and cross, the next three are nearly horizontal and end on the first three right points, the two lowest are slightly curved (the last runs past the right column). The two bracketed labels above are struck/illegible and left out. Still a reading: which strokes start at which left mark (most start just beside the column, not on a mark), and the marks themselves (small ticks, two heavy points). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 259 ppi colour scan (rendered at 350 dpi). Redrawn: the nine strokes were straight lines up to 2 units off their ink; each is now drawn through points read on it, and lies on the ink to within about 0.5 unit. Read on the page: the four upper strokes start beside the left column (at about y = 30.5, 38, 45, 51) and end at about (79.5, 59.4), (68.7, 61.4), (62.1, 58.7), (57.9, 61.1); the fourth (blue) crosses the fifth near x = 30; the fifth runs from the second left mark to the first right point; the sixth and seventh end at the hook and at the slash of the right column; the eighth curls down just before the blue blot; the ninth runs past the column and curls up at its end. The marks are drawn as they are instead of as uniform points: on the left a tick at 44, a tick at 55, a heavy vertical blot at 61, a heavy point with a hooked tail at 69, a tick and a short oblique stroke at 81-85; on the right a heavy point with a short tail at 54, a hook ending in a dot at 64-66, a short slash at 73-74.5, a heavy point at 76 and a filled blot at 85. Left out: the two bracketed words above, which are blotted out (crossings-out, not part of the figure), and three faint specks of the left column (at 33, 47 and 89).
